passage: I had five replies drafted, each meaner than the last. I'm Arohi, and that Monday I found out Kamal had walked to the canteen with the new group and never told me, and hadn't answered my messages for a week. My face was hot for hours. In the notes on my phone I wrote things like "Guess I was only useful for your maths notes." I read them out loud to myself in the bathroom mirror and felt powerful for maybe a minute. Then my mother called me for dinner and I realised I was shaking. I didn't send any of them. I slept badly, and by Thursday the anger had gone quieter. I asked myself if Kamal was worth one calm message. I wrote, "I noticed you've been distant. If something's up, tell me." Then I put the phone away.

qa.q: Where did Arohi write the cutting replies?
qa.a: In the notes on Arohi's phone.

qa.q: What was Arohi feeling on Monday, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Furious and hurt. Arohi's face was hot for hours, the mean replies got read aloud in the mirror, and by dinner Arohi was shaking.

qa.q: What did Arohi do to keep some dignity?
qa.a: Arohi did not send the drafts, let the anger settle for a few days, and then sent one calm message before putting the phone away.

qa.q: How might Kamal see Arohi's final message?
qa.a: Perhaps as a surprise, since it is calm and not blaming. It gives Kamal an easy way to explain if Kamal wants to.

grounding: Arohi is furious at being dropped and rehearses cutting replies, then lets the anger cool and sends one calm message.

passage:
Rukmini had dropped Harish without a word. Two years of sitting together in the school bus in Pune, and now she sat with the new girls from the dance club and looked straight past him.
Harish was furious. On the walk home he rehearsed replies in his head. Don't worry, I didn't even notice you were gone. Enjoy your new fake friends. Each one felt sharper than the last. He typed one out, thumb over the send button.
Then his little sister needed help with her maths homework, and by the time he got back to his phone, an hour had passed. The fury had cooled a little. The message looked childish.
He deleted it. He thought about whether the friendship mattered enough for one more try. It did.
He wrote: "Hey, I've missed sitting with you. If something changed, I'd rather hear it from you." He sent it, then put the phone face down and went to play football.

qa.q: Where did Harish and Rukmini sit together for two years?
qa.a: In the school bus in Pune.

qa.q: How did Harish feel on the walk home?
qa.a: He felt furious and hurt at being dropped, rehearsing sharp, cutting replies in his head.

qa.q: What helped Harish keep his dignity?
qa.a: Letting his anger cool for an hour, deleting the cruel message, and sending one calm, honest one instead.

qa.q: How might Rukmini see Harish's calm message?
qa.a: Rukmini may feel guilty or relieved that he wasn't angry, and the calm tone makes it easier for her to reply honestly.

grounding: A teen furious at being dropped by a friend lets the anger cool, deletes a cutting reply and sends one calm message.

passage:
"Pinky di, listen to this. 'Oh, so NOW you have time for your new cricket friends? Hope they're worth it.' Good, na?"
"Who's it for, Divyansh?"
"Sumit. He hasn't replied to me in two weeks. Two weeks! And yesterday he was laughing with the whole cricket gang."
"That must really hurt."
"I'm not hurt. I'm angry."
"Okay. Angry. How will you feel after you send it?"
"Great. For five seconds."
"And after that?"
Divyansh was silent.
"Look, sleep on it. If tomorrow you still care about him, send something calm. If not, don't send anything."
"Why should I be calm? He's the one who dropped me."
"Because you want to be able to look at yourself later, little brother."
Next morning, Divyansh deleted the draft and wrote instead: "Hey, I've missed you. Is everything okay between us?" His hands still felt shaky. But he felt steady.

qa.q: How long had Sumit not replied to Divyansh?
What was Divyansh feeling underneath his anger?
qa.a: He was hurt by Sumit dropping him, even though he insisted he was only angry.
Sleeping on it and sending a calm message the next morning let Divyansh keep his dignity and leave the door open.

qa.q: How does Pinky di see Divyansh's draft?
qa.a: She sees it as something that would feel good briefly but leave him regretful, so she helps him cool down first.

grounding: A teen furious at being dropped lets the anger cool overnight, decides the friendship is worth one calm message and keeps his dignity.
